_note: pip install 'crafter @ git+https://github.com/chengfanbrain/crafter.git@deterministic' -- a fork of 1.8.3 whose single change is that a seed plus an action list replays exactly (see _state_note). Plain 'pip install crafter' runs this config fine and plays identically to a subject, but its blocks cannot be replayed, so a model cannot be given the same episode. This is the paradigm's level 4 (survival), which is stock crafter: hostiles on, health/food/drink/energy decay, death ends the episode, nothing hidden from the HUD. Levels 1-3 freeze or remove parts of that and belong in a gymnasium.Wrapper shipped with the env, not here: an adapter that added them would stop humans and models from playing the same game.
_keys_note: Crafter's Discrete(17) map is 0=noop, 1=move_left, 2=move_right, 3=move_up, 4=move_down, 5=do, 6=sleep, 7=place_stone, 8=place_table, 9=place_furnace, 10=place_plant, 11=make_wood_pickaxe, 12=make_stone_pickaxe, 13=make_iron_pickaxe, 14=make_wood_sword, 15=make_stone_sword, 16=make_iron_sword. Curriculum 'keys' are Discrete action indices and here they restate the adapter default, so all 17 actions are reachable; noop is 'no key held'. On a button box with fewer buttons, cut 'keys' down and cut the Controls text with it, by hand.
_pacing_note: fps is the env step rate, so it sets how fast the survival clock runs against scanner time. Crafter's own interactive player defaults to 5 (run_gui.py, --fps), which is the only human-play cadence the engine documents; 2.5 is the scanner setting, chosen deliberately: 400 ms a decision instead of 200 ms, which is enough time to read the HUD and pick one of 17 actions under button-box constraints, at the cost of halving the game clock so a 300 s block covers half the survival day. turn_based is false on purpose: with hostiles and homeostatic decay, freezing the world until the subject presses a key would remove the survival pressure and decouple game time from scanner time. latched_keys makes each frame prefer a fresh keydown over the held-key poll, so a tap shorter than one frame is not dropped, which is what run_gui.py does. One action per frame, last press wins.
_score_note: show_score draws the achievement count (and the most recent unlock) in the black letterbox bar left of the frame, which crafter's own HUD does not show. It covers no game pixel and reports only values already in info['achievements'], so the model harness can be given the same scalar; if a model is ever evaluated without it, say so, because that is a difference in what the two players can see.
_cue_note: cues turns on the three synthesized sounds in fmri_gym/cues.py, because crafter itself ships none and three outcomes are otherwise invisible in the bore: a blow that landed on a creature without killing it (five bare-handed presses for a zombie), a press the engine refused (no pickaxe for that rock, no table in reach), and a press the rig dropped. score > hit > blocked, at most one a frame, since audio output queues rather than mixes. The cue is decided from the state the engine is about to act on, not by diffing state afterwards, which cannot see a non-lethal blow at all; it is exact because the player updates first every step, and it reads crafter's own collect/place/make tables without touching the world or its RNG. Collecting grass stays silent on purpose: data.yaml gives it probability 0.1, so a press that yields nothing is a failed roll, not a refusal. cue_overlay writes the same feedback as a line of text in the letterbox bar, and it is off here deliberately: the subject has already heard the cue, so the line repeats what it duplicates, and a word appearing in the left margin pulls the eyes off the centre of the frame between presses. agent_play.py turns it on for itself, since a policy cannot hear a sound and would otherwise be told less than the subject was. The columns hit / no_effect / cue / target land in the npz however both flags are set.
_state_note: state_stride 25 = one pickled savestate (~195 KB, 1.2 ms to write and 7.7 ms to load) every 10 s at 2.5 fps, counted per episode. A measured 300 s block on the fork held 33 anchors, 6.3 MB raw and 0.67 MB inside the compressed npz, and every one of them restored and then played its episode out frame-for-frame identically to the seed replay: that is what makes an anchor a branch point a model can be rolled out from. log_frames stores the displayed pixels too, zlib'd per frame (7.0 KB median in daylight; crafter mixes per-pixel noise into the view at night, so the 34 night frames of that block reached 189 KB, and the block came to 756 frames / 11.2 MB of pixels in a 10.2 MB npz). Frames are kept even though the fork replays exactly, because they are the record that does not depend on whoever opens the block later having the fork installed. On stock crafter they are the only record: it rebalances creatures every tenth step by iterating a Python set of objects, so the despawn choice follows object id() and two runs of the same seed and actions diverge (measured: step 69 of a 300-action check, and most restored anchors within tens of steps). Terrain is identical either way; creatures are not.
_trigger_note: The trigger phase sits under the instructions, not above them, so the scan starts after the subject has finished reading. With the trigger first, the instruction screen (which waits for SPACE) would be inside the run: the run's length in volumes and the onset of every phase after it would depend on how long the reading took. Below the trigger everything is on a fixed schedule, and the number of volumes this config produces is the same for every subject.
_iti_note: end_hold / iti / iti_cue reproduce the rig's structure between rounds (core.py: ITI_RANGE = (4.0, 12.0), the death hold of --death-hold-s 1.2; frontend_pygame.py turns the marker red --cue-s before the next round). The frame that ended the episode holds 1.2 s, so the subject reads what killed them instead of the next world appearing on it; then a blank of 4 to 12 s, drawn uniformly per interval, red for its last second. The jitter is what makes the episode onsets estimable: at one fixed gap every onset would fall at the same phase of every TR. One deviation, deliberate: the held frame is not tinted red (core.py:_death_tint). Stock crafter draws a health bar, so the tint has nothing left to say here, and it would put a colour change into a frame that the replay has to reproduce. The next world is generated inside the blank, not after the cue: crafter's terrain generation blocks for 2.3 to 2.7 s (measured), and waiting for it after the red cross would mean the cross had already announced an episode that was not ready. So the blank is the length it says it is; at the 4 s low end the cross is white for about half a second before it turns red, and the manifest logs what each build cost as the interval's 'built'.
_agent_note: agent_play.py replays this same config with a policy instead of a subject, on the block's own episode seeds, and writes the identical npz schema plus a 'policy' field. That is the only model condition this rig owns: same worlds, played from scratch. Rolling a model out from a human's savestate anchor, or reading a VLM's forward pass over a human's frames, consumes these npz files from outside and does not belong here.
